title: Folic acid supplementation to prevent neural tube defects: updated evidence report and systematic review for the US Preventive Services Task Force
authors: Viswanathan M, Urrutia RP, Hudson KN, Middleton JC, Kahwati LC
population: Limited update: English-language randomised and cohort studies from very highly developed countries published July 2015 to July 2021, surveillance to February 2023; 12 observational studies for benefit and 9 studies for harms
funder: This research was funded under contract 75Q80120D00007, Task Order 01, from the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ), US Department of Health and Human Services, under a contract to support the USPSTF. Investigators worked with USPSTF members and AHRQ staff to develop the scope, analytic framework, and key questions; AHRQ had no role in study selection, quality assessment, or synthesis.
result: Results read from the published abstract. Three new studies (990,372 participants) addressed neural tube defects; one cohort found aRR 0.54 (95% CI 0.31 to 0.91) for use before pregnancy, 0.62 (0.39 to 0.97) during and 0.49 (0.29 to 0.83) before and during, only in 2006-2013 and not 1999-2005. Harms were limited to multiple gestation (1 randomised trial, 431 participants), autism spectrum disorder (7 observational studies, 761,125) and maternal cancer (1 observational study, 429,004); none reported statistically significant harm.
